title_clean: A Different Take on Open Interest Analysis
summary: Explains open interest from the seller's perspective: max-OI put = support and max-OI call = resistance because option SELLERS put up large margin (~1.2 lakh/lot vs a buyer's few thousand) and carry unlimited risk, so the market weights their conviction. Warns max-OI strikes migrate intramonth as sellers adjust.
lessons: Max-OI put strike is support only because sellers - who risk unlimited loss and post big margin - are concentrated there.
OI is contracts on both sides: every lot has a bear (buyer) and a bull (seller); analysts trust the seller's wallet.
Max-OI support/resistance is dynamic: after a 200-400 point fall, sellers shift OI to lower strikes.
Old vs new NSE sites differ only in shares-vs-contracts units (contract multiplier), not in data.

Selling one Nifty lot required ~1.2 lakh margin (Dec 2020)

quotes: Options is a game where there is no level playing field - the buyer risks a few thousand, the seller risks lakhs with unlimited downside.

summary: Call-option basics via a cricket-betting analogy: buyer pays 20 (premium) betting a batsman crosses 100 (strike); profit begins only above 120 (breakeven = strike + premium); loss capped at premium. Also maps expiry (T20 deadline), multiple strikes, and the key caveat: cricket scores only rise, markets move both ways.
lessons: Option buyer: limited risk (premium), theoretically unlimited reward.
Breakeven = strike + premium paid; profit starts only beyond it.
Every strike is a separate market - a chain of simultaneous bets.
The cricket analogy fails in one crucial way: markets retrace, scores do not - direction can reverse before expiry.

title_clean: My View Went Terribly Wrong, Still Made 1.5 Lakhs - Options Firefighting
summary: Live firefighting case study: a short Bajaj Finance/Finserv future plus sold call went against the position as the stock jumped 5% (4,900 to 5,150). Rescue: laddered put sales (4,500/4,700/4,800/4,900/5,000/5,200 strikes), added long January future, sold 5,500 call; ~1 crore additional margin deployed; position closed +1.49 lakh. Plus market-order pattern and VIX-decay outlook.
lessons: Firefighting works only with reserve capital: this rescue needed roughly 1 crore against a 3.5-4 lakh drawdown.
Scale into rescue in ladders (multiple strikes/quantities), not one desperate ticket.
Converting a losing directional short into a hedged combo (long future + sold call + sold puts) can cap damage.
Intraday 100+ point falls that recover are put-selling windows; retail sells first, institutions stabilize.
India VIX typically decays 5-10% in a series' final two weeks - option premiums collapse with it.

title_clean: Don't Buy Majesco Shares - Dividend Stripping Explained
summary: Majeco declared a 9,740% dividend (974/share, near the market price) while selling its business. Debunks the buy-collect-dividend-book-loss tax play: dividend stripping rules disallow the short-term capital loss if bought within 3 months before record date and sold within 3 months after; and dividends are taxed at slab (35-42%) vs 15% STCG - the loss-setoff scheme is both illegal and uneconomic.
lessons: Dividend stripping (buy for dividend, book the price-drop loss, offset it) is expressly disallowed by tax rules.
Dividends are taxed at your slab; short-term capital gains at a lower fixed rate - selling before the record date is often cheaper.
If a deal looks like free money, it is already priced in - ask who is selling to you.
Special dividends usually signal asset sales/wind-downs; the ex-dividend price drop can be near-total.

title_clean: Nifty P/E at 37 - Market Crash Very Soon?
summary: Nifty P/E hit a record 37.16 (P/B 3.82, dividend yield 1.18). Argues crash calls from P/E alone are wrong: P/E = price/EPS, and COVID-crushed EPS inflated the ratio. P/E can normalize via falling prices OR recovering earnings - shows Maruti EPS -8 to +46, ONGC collapse; if earnings double, P/E halves without any fall.
lessons: P/E has two levers: price and earnings; focusing on only one while predicting crashes is a category error.
Distressed EPS makes P/E meaningless (zero/negative earnings = infinite P/E at any price).
A ratio can normalize without a crash if earnings recover - the 2020 P/E spike was a denominator artifact.
Trend is your friend until it bends: do not short a market merely because a single valuation metric is stretched.

title_clean: The Right Way to Interpret Put-Call Ratio (PCR)
summary: Standard PCR (total put OI / total call OI = 1.81) screams crash territory (>1.7 historically preceded crashes; <0.8 marked bottoms). But far strikes pollute the ratio: he recomputes using only strikes within the month's plausible range (12,800-14,200): put OI 1.67 cr vs call 1.49 cr = PCR 1.12 - mildly bullish, no crash signal.
lessons: Raw PCR is distorted by far-OTM strikes nobody expects to trade - filter to the plausible monthly range.
Rule of thumb: PCR >1.7 = crash risk, PCR <0.8 = bottoming zone; between them, no signal.
Range width for filtering: about 1,000 points at month start, 700-800 by mid-month.
A filtered PCR of ~1.1-1.2 reads as mildly bullish, not bearish.

strategies.name: Range-filtered PCR
strategies.construction: Sum put OI and call OI only for strikes within expected monthly range (spot +/-1,000 early in month, +/-700-800 mid-month); PCR = put OI / call OI
strategies.numbers: Dec 2020: raw PCR 1.81 vs filtered 1.12 (put 1.67 cr, call 1.49 cr in 12,800-14,200)
strategies.best_regime: Weekly/mid-month sentiment read before taking directional or option-selling positions
strategies.adjustments: Recompute as the expected range narrows through the month
strategies.risks: Range guess can be wrong in trending/volatile months; still an OI-based sentiment proxy, not a timing signal
